🏰 Vienna, every building standing today by year of construction — 1840 → 2025.

Until 1857 the old city was still locked inside its 16th-century bastions, with an empty glacis around them. On 20 December 1857 Emperor Franz Joseph ordered the walls torn down: demolition began in 1858, the Ringstraße opened on 1 May 1865, and the last bastion fell in 1875. The Opera, Parliament, City Hall and Votivkirche rose on the old glacis, while the Gründerzeit filled the suburbs. Then came the council housing of Red Vienna in the 1920s and 30s, post-war rebuilding, and the towers across the Danube.

📊 Data: City of Vienna open data (CC BY 4.0): 3D building model, MA 19 building inventory, survey of the 16th–19th-century fortifications. 20% of the buildings shown have an exact year and 52% a recorded building period, spread over its years; the remaining 28%, mostly post-war housing, are estimated from Statistik Austria's count of buildings by period in each district (2023). Heights exaggerated.
